# Introduction and Objective

Willow and Rock Ptarmigan are primary prey sources for the Gyrfalcon, a declining Arctic raptor species. For this research project, I will aim to estimate annual ptarmigan abundance to support PhD student Michael Henderson's research linking adult survival of Gyrfalcons to ptarmigan numbers in Alaska along the Seward Peninsula.

# Data

Since 2016, the Peregrine Fund has conducted annual distance sampling surveys along 10 mi road transects in the Seward Peninsula of Alaska. Each transect was surveyed twice yearly. Surveys were completed by two observers scanning for ptarmigan in a vehicle. When ptarmigan were spotted, observers would tally birds and record distance to the bird with rangefinders. Data from 2016-2026 was cleaned and combined into one csv by Kara Beer. The first rows of the dataset and its dimensions are shown here:

```{r pulldata, echo = FALSE}
# set path to where you can access your data #
# Note that the path will be different for your.#
datapath <- datadir <- paste( getwd(), "/Data/", sep = "" )
# load ptarmigan raw detection data
detdf <- read.csv( file = paste( datadir, "2026-07-23_all_prey_data.csv", sep = ""),
                   header = TRUE )
#view
head( detdf ); dim( detdf )
```
## Cleaning

First, I removed all observations that are not of Rock or Willow Ptarmigan.
```{r cleannonptarm, include = FALSE}

#database has observations that are not ptarmigan. view all the species in the species column
unique(detdf$species)

#new dataframe with only relevant columns and only for ptarmigan obs.
ptarmdetdf <- detdf %>% 
  dplyr::select(year, round, observer1, observer2, species, cluster_size, distance) %>% #select relevant columns (cluster_size = ptarmigan count),
  dplyr::filter(., species == "WIPT" | species == "ROPT" )  #filter out rows that are not willow and rock ptarmigan counts

#view
head(ptarmdetdf); dim(ptarmdetdf)

```
This removed *`r nrow( detdf ) - nrow(ptarmdetdf)`* observations.

In my initial data exploration, I discovered that the data in the distance row was character class instead of numeric class due to the inclusion of values such as "<100," ">1200," and "U." My next cleaning step is to turn the column into numeric values and filter out the NAs converted from the greater than, less than values, and U values.

```{r cleandistance, include = FALSE}

# First, check class of distance column
sapply(ptarmdetdf$distance, class)
# all character

#convert to numeric
ptarmdetdf$distance <- as.numeric(ptarmdetdf$distance)

#check again to make sure
sapply(ptarmdetdf$distance, class)
#all numeric

#drop all rows with NAs
cleandetdf <- ptarmdetdf %>%
  drop_na(.,"distance")

#check for NAs
sum(is.na(cleandetdf$distance))
#0 NAs

#view
head(cleandetdf); dim(cleandetdf)

```

This cleaning step removed *`r nrow( ptarmdetdf ) - nrow(cleandetdf)`* rows.

## Visualization

Key to distance sampling models is fitting distance sampling curves to detection of ptarmigan by distance. First, I will create histograms of distance to ptarmigan for each observer pair by year for each round of surveys to determine the type of curve that will be used in the model. 

First, I added a column to my dataframe with each unique pair of observers.

```{r obspair, include = FALSE}

#make a column with each unique pair of observers
cleandetdf$obsv_pair <- apply(cleandetdf[, c("observer1", "observer2")], 1, function(x) {
   last <- word(x, -1)
   tolower(paste(sort(last), collapse = "-"))
 })

#view
cleandetdf$obsv_pair

#what are the unique observer pairs?
unique(cleandetdf$obsv_pair)

#check for NAs just in case
sum(is.na(cleandetdf$obsv_pair))
  
```
The unique observer pairs are: `r unique(cleandetdf$obsv_pair)`

First, I visualized the general histogram of all distances ptarmigans are detected at. 
```{r allhist, echo = FALSE}

#plot histogram of distances grouped by species
ggplot( cleandetdf, aes(x = distance, fill = species)) +
  theme_classic() +
  geom_histogram()

```

Next, I create two different dataframes for each of the two rounds of surveys.

```{r rounds, include = FALSE}

#just round 1 surveys
det1 <- cleandetdf %>%
  dplyr::filter(., round == "1" )

#view
head(det1); dim(det1)
#2808 rows

#just round 2 surveys
det2 <- cleandetdf %>%
  dplyr::filter(., round == "2" )

#view
head(det2); dim(det2)
#2382 rows

```
There are `r nrow(det1)` observations in all round 1 surveys and `r nrow(det2)` observations in all round 2 surveys.

### Round 1 Histograms

Here are the histograms for round 1 of surveys for each observer pair by year.

```{r round1hist, echo = FALSE}

#create an object that stores all unique observer pairs
pairs1 <- c(unique(det1$obsv_pair))
#view
pairs1

#for loop to create histograms of distance by observer pair/year and survey (1st or 2nd)
for( p in 1:length(pairs1) ){
  # create an object with the ggplot so that you can display it 
  # in a loop 
  a <- ggplot( subset(det1, obsv_pair %in% pairs1[p]), aes(x = distance, fill = species) ) + #data subsetted to observer pair by year. plot distance and color code by species.
    theme_bw( base_size = 15 ) + #choose a preset theme
    labs( title = pairs1[p], subtitle = "Round 1" ) + #label graphs using our observer pairs
    geom_histogram() + #plot histogram
    facet_wrap(~year) #plot by survey 1 and 2
    #scale_x_discrete(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(5))
  # display your plot object
  print( a )
}
```

### Round 2 Histograms

Here are the histograms for round 2 of surveys for each observer pair by year.

```{r round2hist, echo = FALSE}

#create an object that stores all unique observer pairs
pairs2 <- c(unique(det2$obsv_pair))
#view
pairs2

#for loop to create histograms of distance by observer pair/year and survey (1st or 2nd)
for( p in 1:length(pairs2) ){
  # create an object with the ggplot so that you can display it 
  # in a loop 
  a <- ggplot( subset(det2, obsv_pair %in% pairs2[p]), aes(x = distance, fill = species) ) + #data subsetted to observer pair by year. plot distance and color code by species.
    theme_bw( base_size = 15 ) + #choose a preset theme
    labs( title = pairs2[p], subtitle = "Round 2" ) + #label graphs using our observer pairs
    geom_histogram() + #plot histogram
    facet_wrap(~year) #plot by survey 1 and 2
    #scale_x_discrete(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(5))
  # display your plot object
  print( a )
}
```
